# Request a grant from an OSE Fund

Besides expenses and invoices, the Open Collective platform also has a **Request a Grant** option.

Collectives may also request approval for donations to identified nonprofit organizations. This permission is separate from access to the **Request a Grant** feature that this page describes. Open Source Europe (OSE) reviews the beneficiary, purpose, and funding conditions before it accepts an outgoing grant or donation.

The **Request a Grant** feature is not available to all Collectives, and its use must follow specific conditions.

***

## Who can use “Request a Grant”?

* This guide covers grant requests to OSE Funds. Whether a profile can receive grant requests depends on the expense types enabled for it. These expense types alone do not make a request eligible. OSE confirms the right way to submit for the arrangement you agreed.
* The ordinary OSE route is for identified nonprofit organizations, such as foundations, associations sans but lucratif (ASBLs), charities, or nongovernmental organizations (NGOs). OSE must first review and agree to the beneficiary, purpose, and funding conditions.
* Other beneficiaries, including individuals or informal collectives, need a specific assessment by OSE, and OSE does not guarantee to accept them. Contact OSE before you go ahead. A request is not eligible only because the platform offers the feature.

***

## Requirements for submitting a grant request

When a nonprofit uses the **Request a Grant** feature, it must include the following documents:

* Copy of the nonprofit's legal bylaws (*statuts*)
* Signed letter that officially requests the grant and sets out:
  * The amount, purpose, and objectives of the requested funding
  * How the nonprofit plans to use the funds in line with the Fund’s mission
  * The legal name and contact details of the nonprofit organization
* Bank account holder statement of the nonprofit

> These documents help OSE check legal eligibility, check that the request meets the funder requirements, and prepare reporting if needed.

***

## Internal review process

Who selects the projects or beneficiaries depends on the program. The selection roles are agreed with OSE when the Fund is set up. Selection does not replace OSE's review and agreement before payment.

The OSE team reviews all grant requests manually. For an approved nonprofit grant, OSE transfers the funds directly to the nonprofit's official bank account. OSE records the transaction transparently on the Fund page. For other beneficiaries, OSE must first confirm whether it can accept the arrangement, and which documents and payment arrangements it needs.

For questions about an OSE Fund or about who can receive a grant, contact <home@opensourceeurope.org>.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# The partnership

## Legal relationship: indirect representation

The relationship between your Collective and Open Source Europe (OSE) is one of indirect representation (*représentation indirecte* / *middellijke vertegenwoordiging*).

This relationship means the following:

* Your Collective remains fully responsible for its own activities, including legal and tax compliance.
* OSE acts as a fiscal host and intermediary, not as the legal representative or owner of your funds or operations.

> **Danger:** Your Collective must not use OSE's tax identification number, such as its value-added tax (VAT) number, to invoice or to register. If you need a tax number, you are responsible for getting your own tax number under local law.

***

## Invoicing guidelines

Follow these rules to stay compliant with the OSE hosting terms:

* Address invoices to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer for these purchases. Collectives must not ask for invoices in OSE’s legal name or with OSE's VAT number.
* Third parties must treat your Collective as an unincorporated group or individual for VAT purposes.
* If VAT does not apply, the invoice must cite the relevant VAT exemption article.

> **Danger:** If an invoice is wrongly addressed to OSE, the invoice must be canceled and replaced. Repeated errors may lead to the end of your fiscal hosting agreement.

***

## Donations from your Collective

A Collective can make ordinary external donations to identified nonprofit organizations. OSE must first review and approve the beneficiary, purpose, and funding conditions. Contact OSE before you make a commitment or request payment. Other types of recipient require a specific assessment, and OSE does not promise to accept them.

Some funds come under a grant agreement or for a restricted purpose. Before OSE passes on such funds, OSE checks whether the transfer is permitted and which obligations still apply. Any required funder approval must be obtained. A transfer does not automatically release OSE from its responsibilities under the original funding agreement.

After OSE has approved the arrangement, follow these steps:

1. Ask the beneficiary to submit an expense through your Collective's page.
2. Make sure the expense includes the following documents:
   * Signed letter from the beneficiary that confirms the purpose and amount
   * Copy of the beneficiary's incorporation document
   * Bank identification document of the beneficiary

> **Danger:** The ordinary external donation route is for identified nonprofit organizations. Other cases need a specific assessment, and OSE does not accept them automatically. OSE does not treat a payment in exchange for goods, services, or visibility as an ordinary donation. Contact OSE before you make that commitment.

***

## VAT and nonprofit status

For purchases by a Collective, the supplier must issue invoices to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer. Do not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number.

VAT treatment depends on the specific transaction and the rules that apply to it. Do not assume one rule applies to every purchase. Ask the supplier or an accountant about exemptions, reverse charge, or VAT recovery.

> **Note:** For more information, see [VAT in Europe and how it works in OSE](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/the-partnership/vat-in-europe-and-how-it-works-in-ose/).

***

## Questions?

Email OSE any time at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# VAT in Europe and how it works in OSE

## General principles

For purchases made by a Collective, the supplier must issue invoices to the Collective or the person who placed the order. Open Source Europe (OSE) acts only as the payer. Do not ask for these invoices in OSE’s legal name or with OSE's value-added tax (VAT) number. This page does not cover purchases that OSE contracts directly for its own needs.

VAT treatment depends on the transaction and the rules that apply to it. Hosting with OSE does not by itself decide whether VAT must be charged, whether an exemption applies, or whether VAT can be recovered.

***

## VAT within the same country

Ask the supplier to apply the VAT treatment that fits the purchase and the actual customer. If the VAT treatment on the invoice is unclear, ask the supplier to explain it or consult an accountant. Do not assume that every invoice without VAT is wrong.

***

## Cross-border VAT and reverse charge

Cross-border rules differ by transaction, by the status of the parties, and by the countries involved. Hosting with OSE does not mean that reverse charge always applies. Hosting with OSE also does not mean that reverse charge can never apply.

For a specific purchase, ask the supplier or an accountant to confirm the treatment that applies. Do not give OSE’s VAT number for the Collective’s purchase.

The following pages give official guidance:

* [VAT rules and rates – Your Europe](https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/finance-and-tax/vat/vat-rules-rates/index_en.htm)
* [Cross-border VAT – Your Europe](https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/finance-and-tax/vat/cross-border-vat/index_en.htm)

***

## Summary

The following points sum up this page:

* Put the Collective’s name, or the name of the person who placed the order, on the invoice. Do not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number.
* Ask the supplier or an accountant about VAT treatment, exemptions, reverse charge, or recovery for the specific purchase.
* Payment or reimbursement still depends on OSE’s document checks, the funding conditions, and the funds available.

***

## Questions?

For OSE’s requirements on submitting invoices and on payment, contact <home@opensourceeurope.org>. For the tax treatment of your own purchase or situation, consult the supplier or an accountant.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Applying for grants

Use this guide when a funder may support your Collective through Open Source Europe (OSE). Your Collective leads the application and the project. OSE reviews its own role and commitments.

## The grant journey

1. Before you submit, check the funder's requirements and contact OSE. If the application names OSE as recipient or signatory, OSE must review and accept that role before submission.
2. If you get the grant, share the grant agreement and arrange the necessary agreements and payment instructions with OSE.
3. When the funds arrive, use the Collective budget in line with the funding conditions. A promised grant is not an available balance.
4. During the project, prepare activity reports and project monitoring. OSE provides the accounting information it holds and validates anything that binds OSE.

The following sections give the details of the agreement, communication, and reporting requirements. See also [hosting fees](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost) and [spending the grant budget](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/).

## Grants through OSE

OSE enables hosted Collectives to receive grants from institutional and philanthropic funders, both in Europe and internationally. The OSE team helps you prepare the arrangements to receive and manage the grant.

> **Danger:** If a grant application names OSE as recipient or signatory, contact OSE before submission, so the team can review and accept OSE's role and commitments.

***

## Initial steps

1. Contact OSE early

   Email <home@opensourceeurope.org> to tell OSE about the grant opportunity. The OSE team helps you check whether the grant is compatible with fiscal hosting through OSE.
2. Check the funder's requirements

   Some funders do not allow grants to fiscally sponsored initiatives. Ask the funder whether it accepts a hosted structure.
3. If your funder is in the U.S., arrange its documentation

   Contact the OSE team to arrange the documentation that your funder requires. For more information, see [Equivalency Determination Certificate](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/).

***

## Grant agreements & receiving funds

1. Share the grant agreement

   The funder provides a grant agreement. The confirmed recipient entity must sign this agreement. Share the agreement with OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org>, or ask the funder to contact OSE directly.
2. Sign the Mandate Agreement

   Your initiative also needs to sign a Mandate Agreement with OSE. This agreement makes the arrangement formal. One signatory from your initiative is enough.
3. Get the bank transfer instructions

   The OSE team provides the right bank transfer instructions for the agreed grant arrangement.
4. Check the available balance

   Once OSE receives the grant, the funds appear on your Collective’s Open Collective page as available balance.

***

## Funder communication

The following points cover how you communicate with funders:

* You can publicly recognize funders on your Collective page. A funder's name appears in your list of contributors unless the funder chooses to remain anonymous.
* Keep your funders informed with regular updates on the Open Collective platform.
* If funders send requests or messages to OSE, OSE forwards them to your initiative for follow-up.

***

## Grant reporting

The Collective prepares activity reports and project monitoring. OSE provides the accounting information it holds and validates statements or commitments that bind OSE. Follow the reporting requirements and deadlines of the grant agreement.

***

## Get help

The Collective leads its own fundraising. OSE may occasionally share opportunities or make introductions when it has capacity. OSE does not promise a structured fundraising service or funding success. For questions about how to receive and administer a grant, contact <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

## Hosting fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost).


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Contributions in cryptocurrencies

Collectives hosted by Open Source Europe (OSE) can receive cryptocurrency donations through the established route:

Every.org → Myriad USA → Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCEF) → OSE → the Collective’s budget on Open Collective.

## Set up the donation page

Contact OSE first at <home@opensourceeurope.org>. The OSE team creates and hosts an Every.org page for your Collective. The team also provides the applicable instructions, documents, fees, and transfer information. Every.org is the required starting point for this cryptocurrency route.

## Receive and transfer funds

Cryptocurrency is converted into conventional currency before it is allocated to the Collective. OSE does not pay cryptocurrency out to the Collective.

The Collective may ask OSE at any time to transfer the funds received on Every.org to its Open Collective budget. The OSE team handles the intermediary steps. A request does not mean an immediate payout. No fixed twice-yearly transfer schedule applies.

## Fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost). Before you send funds, contact OSE for the applicable processing, conversion, and intermediary costs. Do not assume a combined fee or transfer date.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Fundraising tools & resources

This page lists more ways to raise funds.

Open Collective includes crowdfunding tools and is the usual way to raise funds for a Collective hosted by Open Source Europe (OSE).

## External platforms

OSE considers external platforms, such as Patreon, Ko-fi, and GoFundMe, case by case. Contact OSE before you set up a campaign to receive funds through OSE. The OSE team checks payout arrangements, available records, and any promised benefits. Then the team confirms whether OSE can accept the setup. Do not assume that donations reach your OSE Collective when you choose an organization with a similar name.

## Supported routes

The following routes have their own guides:

* [GitHub Sponsors](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/setting-up-github-sponsors/)
* [U.S. tax-deductible donations](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/)
* [Cryptocurrency donations](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/contributions-in-cryptocurrencies/)

## Fundraising support

The Collective leads its fundraising. OSE may occasionally share opportunities or make introductions when it has capacity. OSE does not guarantee funding or provide a standard fundraising service.

For an unidentified incoming payment, [contact OSE](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/contact-us/) with its reference, so the team can find out where the payment should go. This process is separate from how OSE handles the balances of inactive Collectives.

# Financial contributions – how to donate

Guides for donors and financial contributors.

Choose the route that matches the donor or funding arrangement. For an ordinary contribution, start on the Collective's Open Collective page. The section "Accepted payment methods" describes the card, PayPal, and bank transfer options.

## Find the right route

The following table links each task to its guide:

| What you want to do                    | Guide                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

Before you choose a route, check the [current hosting fees](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost). Contact Open Source Europe (OSE) before you set up an external collection or promise goods, services, or other benefits in return for funding.

## Why donate through Open Source Europe

Through OSE, donors can support Collectives transparently and securely. Hosted Collectives don't need their own bank account or legal entity: OSE receives and manages the funds for them. Donors can also choose to be publicly acknowledged on the Collective’s profile.

***

## Accepted payment methods

You can make a contribution through:

* Credit or debit card
* PayPal
* Bank transfer (SEPA or international)

> **Caution:** When you make a bank transfer, include the name of the Collective and your order number in the payment reference. If you cannot, contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org> with your transaction details, so OSE can assign the payment correctly.

***

## Information required

When you donate, the donation form may ask for:

* Your full name
* Your email address
* Your organization name (if applicable)
* Your payment method details

***

## Bank transfer instructions

To contribute by bank transfer, follow the step-by-step [wire transfer instructions](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/wire-transfer-instructions-via-open-collective-platform/).

***

## Tax-deductible giving

U.S. donors can use the established Myriad → OCEF → OSE route for tax-deductible giving, subject to applicable tax rules. Contact OSE before you pay, so that OSE can organize the right route. For more information, see [U.S. giving](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/).

***

## Get help

If you’re not sure which method to use, or you want to check your transaction, contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

## Hosting fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost).

# Refunds

Can I refund a donation or get a refund for one I have made?

## Can I request a refund for a donation?

Yes, under certain conditions. Open Source Europe (OSE) can process refunds for contributions made by credit card, bank transfer, or PayPal.

### Refund timeframes

For a credit card or bank transfer contribution, you can request a refund within 90 days of the contribution date. For a PayPal contribution, you can request a refund within 60 days of the contribution date.

> **Danger:** Refunds go only to the original payment method. For card payments processed through Stripe, Stripe and the card issuer route the refund, including when the original card has expired or been replaced. OSE reviews the request and starts an approved refund. OSE does not control how the bank handles the funds.

***

## How to request a refund

Contact the Collective administrators first. They forward your request to OSE. If the administrators do not respond, contact OSE directly at <home@opensourceeurope.org>. A request does not guarantee a refund. Include the following details:

* URL of the donation (for example, `https://opencollective.com/europe/contributions/528520`)
* Date and amount of the transaction
* Reason for the refund request

> **Danger:** OSE reviews each refund request. OSE may decline the refund if the contribution was authorized and the funds were already used for the Collective's activities.

***

## Refund processing times

OSE first reviews the refund request. If OSE approves the request, OSE starts the refund. The time it takes for the funds to reach you then depends on the payment method, payment provider, and bank. OSE does not guarantee a fixed processing or receipt date.

These processing steps are separate from the request deadlines in "Refund timeframes": 90 days for card or bank-transfer contributions and 60 days for PayPal.

***

## Additional information

The following points also apply to refunds:

* Refunds go only to the original payment method.
* The handling of an expired card or closed account depends on the payment provider and bank. An expired card or closed account is not an automatic reason for OSE to declare a refund impossible.
* For contributions made by manual bank transfer, the administrators forward the request to OSE to discuss refund options. If the administrators do not respond, contact OSE directly.

***

## Get help

If you have questions about refunds or need more help, contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

# Setting up GitHub Sponsors

This guide shows how to connect GitHub Sponsors for Organizations to your Collective.

## Choose your starting point

Pick the case that matches your project:

* For a new organization profile, follow First activation. Have the URL of your Collective hosted by Open Source Europe (OSE) ready. Use an organization owner account with two-factor authentication.
* If you are already sponsored through another host, start with Move GitHub Sponsors from another host. A move on Open Collective does not move your Sponsors setup automatically.
* For a personal GitHub account, discuss the arrangement with OSE. The activation steps on this page are for organizations.

The result is a Sponsors profile for your project that uses OSE's fiscal-host route. GitHub reviews the profile first. If the host label or payout setup is unclear, contact OSE before you continue.

Use GitHub Sponsors for your project with OSE as fiscal host and your Collective on Open Collective as the destination for its budget.

## First activation for a GitHub organization

1. Check that your project has a Collective hosted by OSE. The person who configures Sponsors must be an owner of the project’s GitHub organization and have two-factor authentication enabled.
2. Visit [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors), choose **Get sponsored**, and select the project’s own GitHub organization.
3. Select **This organization is using a fiscal host**, then select the host entry for OSE. If the label is unclear, contact OSE before you continue. The public GitHub guide may still show the earlier name, Open Collective Europe.
4. In **Fiscal host project profile URL**, enter your Collective’s Open Collective URL, for example `https://opencollective.com/{COLLECTIVE_SLUG}`. Do not enter OSE’s GitHub organization URL in this field.
5. Complete the project profile and request GitHub approval. Activation depends on GitHub’s review, and there is no promised date for approval.

OSE’s GitHub organization is [opensourceeurope](https://github.com/opensourceeurope). You configure sponsorship for your own project through the fiscal-host route. Do not set up your own Stripe account for that route. If you see a payout setup step you did not expect, contact OSE.

GitHub also supports personal sponsored accounts. This guide covers the setup for organizations. For a personal account, discuss your case with OSE.

## Move GitHub Sponsors from another host

Contact OSE to organize a change from another fiscal host. When you move your Collective on Open Collective, its GitHub Sponsors host does not change automatically. OSE supports you through the process and works with GitHub where needed. Do not assume the migration is complete until the GitHub setup has been confirmed.

## Fees and sponsorship benefits

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost). GitHub’s own fees are separate. For more information, see GitHub’s [current fee guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/sponsoring-open-source-contributors/about-sponsorships-fees-and-taxes).

If you plan to promise goods, services, or other benefits to sponsors, contact OSE before you commit or receive payment. GitHub’s tier features do not automatically make an arrangement acceptable to OSE.

## Official instructions

GitHub describes the setup in these guides:

* [Using a fiscal host](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/receiving-sponsorships-through-github-sponsors/using-a-fiscal-host-to-receive-github-sponsors-payouts)
* [Setting up Sponsors for an organization](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/receiving-sponsorships-through-github-sponsors/setting-up-github-sponsors-for-your-organization)

If you have questions, contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

# Wire transfer instructions through the Open Collective platform

This option is available for all funds.

## Contribute by bank transfer

If you prefer to contribute to a Collective by bank transfer, Open Source Europe (OSE) has a simple process for this payment method.

***

## Step-by-step guide

1. Start the donation
   * Go to the page of the Collective you want to support.
   * Click the **Contribute** button.
   * Select **Bank Transfer** as your payment method.
2. Get the transfer instructions
   * After you confirm your contribution, you'll get an email with:
     * OSE's bank account details
     * A unique **Order Number** for your contribution
3. Make the bank transfer
   * Start the transfer from your bank, and make sure you:
     * Use exactly the bank details provided.
     * Include the **Order Number** and the Collective's name in the payment reference.

> **Caution:** If you leave out the Order Number or the Collective's name, OSE may need longer to allocate your funds.

4. Wait for the contribution to appear
   * Allow up to seven business days for the contribution to appear in the Collective's budget. Count from the date you send the bank transfer. This time is an estimate, not a guarantee. If the contribution has not appeared after seven business days, contact OSE as described in Troubleshooting.
   * The contribution appears in the Collective's budget once the OSE hosting team confirms receipt and allocates the transfer to the Collective.

***

## Visual guide

[Image removed: The Open Collective thank-you page after a contribution, with a pending notice and payment instructions that give the amount, IBAN, BIC, and order reference for the bank transfer]

[Image removed: The confirmation email, with the bank transfer instructions: amount, IBAN, BIC, order reference, and recipient address]

*Example of the confirmation screen with the bank transfer details.*

***

## Troubleshooting

Use the following checks when a bank transfer does not go as expected.

### The instruction email did not arrive

Check your spam or junk folder. If the email is not there, contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org>.

### The funds are not in the budget after seven business days

Check that the payment reference included the correct Order Number and the Collective's name. Then give OSE the following details:

* Transaction receipt
* Amount sent
* Date of the transfer
* Sender's name

Send these details and any supporting documents by email to <home@opensourceeurope.org>. OSE then helps you. Do not send them through Slack or Discord.

## Hosting fees

See the [current OSE fee reference](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost).

# Open Source Europe documentation

Practical guidance for joining Open Source Europe (OSE), receiving funds, and managing your Collective.

If you are new to OSE: [Start your application](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/). If OSE has already accepted you: [Follow your first steps](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/basics/).

## Choose your task

- [Join OSE](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/): Check whether hosting fits your project and prepare your application.
- [Run your Collective](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/basics/): Start after acceptance, manage your budget, and keep your contacts up to date.
- [Receive funds](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/): Choose a donation route, receive a grant, or connect GitHub Sponsors.
- [Pay and get reimbursed](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/): Choose an invoice or reimbursement and prepare your payment request.
- [Fees and hosting rules](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/): Understand hosting costs and find answers about your arrangement with OSE.
- [Get help](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/contact-us/): Find the right contact for a question, a payment issue, or a sensitive concern.

## Common tasks

The following pages cover common tasks:

* [Check project eligibility](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/eligibility/)
* [Review hosting fees](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost)
* [Choose invoice or reimbursement](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements/)
* [Apply for a grant](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/applying-for-grants/)
* [Connect GitHub Sponsors](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/setting-up-github-sponsors/)
* [Arrange U.S. donations](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/)
* [Make an outgoing grant or donation](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/request-a-grant-for-nonprofits-only/)
* [Move or close a Collective](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/fiscal-hosting-faqs/)

## Understand OSE

Read [what OSE offers](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/), explore [budget decisions](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/guides/deciding-on-how-to-use-your-money/), or consult the [payment FAQ](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/expenses-and-getting-paid-faqs/).

For a safeguarding concern, go directly to the [safeguarding policy and contacts](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/safeguarding-policy/).

Open Source Europe is a Belgian association (ASBL/vzw). Its tech platform lets open source groups raise and spend funds in full transparency.

### Mission

OSE supports movements and decentralized communities with the infrastructure they need to:

* Launch new projects
* Manage and oversee financial operations
* Keep open source initiatives legally and fiscally compliant

If you run an open source project, OSE helps you reach your goals. OSE takes on the administrative work of managing your funds.

OSE also works with foundations and philanthropists to set up dedicated funds. These funds let them re-grant resources to open source initiatives globally.

***

### How OSE can help

#### For open source Collectives

When your group partners with OSE, it can:

* Launch and manage projects without having to incorporate a separate legal entity
* Simplify financial operations with the Open Collective platform
* Connect with global philanthropic opportunities and corporate sponsors

#### For foundations and philanthropists

OSE offers professional help to:

* Support transparent re-granting processes
* Create and manage philanthropic funds
* Support open source initiatives on a global scale through a recognized European structure

***

### Get started

The following links take you to the next step:

* [Apply for hosting](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply)
* [Join the Discord server](https://discord.gg/TmbRzFBqBa)
* [Contact OSE](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org)

# Terms of Service

## Hosting agreement

Hosting with Open Source Europe is governed by the association's Terms of Hosting.

The [Terms of Hosting for the association](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15Wkvfn5ou-is_eUjautjDv4JZ-tiY2-c/edit) are the reference document for this hosting relationship. [Contact the team](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org) to obtain the applicable version and any additional agreement relevant to your project.

## Main responsibilities

This overview explains the main points of the association's Terms of Hosting. It does not replace or amend the agreement.

* Your initiative remains responsible for its activities and related obligations. Hosting does not make the initiative a legal extension of the association.
* The association receives and administers funds on the initiative's behalf through an indirect representation relationship.
* The initiative retains its intellectual property unless a separate agreement provides otherwise.
* The initiative cannot bind the association to an agreement with a third party without prior written approval.
* Contributions and expenses must be recorded transparently on the platform. Expense requests require supporting documents and review.
* Funds must support the initiative's stated purpose. The initiative must keep its description up to date.
* Administrative fees and directly related processing expenses are deducted according to the applicable agreement.

OSE recommends that you publish a public update on your Collective page at least once a year. This is not a general hosting obligation. Any specific reporting requirements in your applicable agreement or funding arrangement still apply.

## Starting, changing, or ending the arrangement

Contact the team before you enter into a grant agreement or make a commitment on behalf of the association. Also contact the team before a significant change to your project's mission or activities. Collectives manage routine adjustments themselves. Any specific approval requirements for contracts and funding arrangements still apply.

The Terms of Hosting provide for termination with **30 days' written notice**. Valid outstanding expenses and any remaining balance are handled under the agreement's termination provisions. A remaining balance is not automatically available for distribution to individual administrators.

For current guidance on contributions, see [Contributions FAQ](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/contributions-faq/). If your planned activity raises a question about the scope of the hosting agreement, contact the team before proceeding.

## Contact

<home@opensourceeurope.org>

# Equivalency Determination certificate

## Grants from U.S. foundations

Open Source Europe (OSE) helps hosted projects receive grants from U.S. foundations through an Equivalency Determination (ED) arrangement.

Contact the OSE team before you apply. The OSE team coordinates with the funder, provides the relevant documentation, and arranges for the grant to reach your project.

## Prepare a grant application

Contact <home@opensourceeurope.org> early, with:

* The funder's name and the project that the grant is for
* Proposed amount, purpose, and application deadline
* Any eligibility requirements or draft grant agreement

The team provides the current ED documentation and confirms the details to use in the grant agreement. An ED does not guarantee that a particular funder or grant program will accept an application.

## Donations from individuals

An ED is different from the route for U.S. tax-deductible donations through Myriad USA. For more information, see [Tax-deductible giving for U.S. donors](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/).

## Documentation for the funder

Open Collective Europe Foundation holds the ED used for this arrangement. On this route, the foundation receives the grant and transfers it to OSE for your project. The OSE team coordinates these steps.


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# What OSE offers

Open Source Europe (OSE) provides the legal and financial infrastructure that open source projects need. OSE services let you focus on your code instead of paperwork.

OSE offers one core service: fiscal hosting. Fiscal hosting includes everything you need to run your project professionally.

***

## Core infrastructure

### A legal home for your project

Operate under OSE, a Belgian nonprofit association (ASBL/vzw). Your project can then receive funds, manage contracts, and act as a single legal entity, without the work and cost of creating its own.

### Transparent financial tools

Use the Open Collective platform to manage your budget, receive donations, and pay contributors and expenses with full transparency. Your community and backers can see every transaction in real time, which builds trust and accountability.

### Access to grants and funding

Many foundations and companies want to fund open source but find it hard to support unincorporated groups. OSE acts as a trusted intermediary, so your project can receive grants from these larger institutional funders.

***

## Why choose fiscal hosting

Fiscal hosting suits open source projects that want to focus on their mission without the admin work of formal incorporation. Fiscal hosting gives you:

* Immediate legitimacy, with high-level compliance for corporate sponsors
* Less overhead, with no need for your own accounting or legal teams
* A place among open source projects that share the same infrastructure

***

## Get started

To join the community of open source projects that OSE hosts:

* [Apply for hosting](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply)
* [Join the OSE Discord](https://discord.gg/TmbRzFBqBa)
* [Contact the OSE team](mailto:home@opensourceeurope.org)

# Tax-deductible giving for U.S. donors

## An established route for U.S. giving

U.S. individuals and businesses can support Collectives hosted by Open Source Europe (OSE) through Myriad USA → Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCEF) → OSE. This established arrangement allows U.S. tax-deductible donations, within the limits of the applicable tax rules. The donor’s actual deduction depends on their circumstances.

## Choose the appropriate donation route

Contact OSE at <home@opensourceeurope.org> before payment, and give the name of the Collective you want to support. The team organizes the route, reference, documents, applicable costs, and transfer arrangements.

* For regular fundraising from U.S. donors, an Every.org page organized with OSE is the preferred option. Funds follow Every.org → Myriad → OCEF → OSE.
* A donor who gives a larger donation gives directly to Myriad, without Every.org. Funds then follow Myriad → OCEF → OSE. Ask the team for the correct instructions. This page gives no fixed amount threshold.

A donation through the ordinary Open Collective checkout does not automatically use this arrangement. Confirm which organization issues the donation documentation for the route you choose.

The [current OSE hosting fees](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost) apply. The team confirms any additional costs of the route.

## Other cases

If the tax-deductible route for your circumstances is not confirmed yet, contact OSE before you give, and check the available route and documents. OSE does not guarantee an individual tax benefit.

Cryptocurrency donations must start on Every.org. For more information, see [Cryptocurrency contributions](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/contributions-in-cryptocurrencies/).

For grants from U.S. foundations, see [Equivalency Determination certificate](https://www.opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/).

For more information about Myriad, see the [Myriad FAQ](https://myriadusa.org/about/faqs/) and the [Myriad ways to give](https://myriadusa.org/waystogive/).


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# The Open Collective platform

Open Collective is a shared tool to manage contributions, expenses, and grants with full transparency.

## A transparent financial and community management tool

Open Collective is a digital platform that lets hosted initiatives and philanthropic partners raise, manage, and distribute funds with full transparency. Each group or fund hosted by Open Source Europe (OSE) gets its own public page, with tools to:

* Accept donations by credit card, PayPal, or bank transfer, and manage grants
* Submit, approve, and reimburse expenses directly on the platform
* Display a transparent budget that shows all income and expenditures in real time, which builds trust and accountability
* Post updates, host events, and share progress with supporters

These tools in one place make financial administration simpler and help your initiative or fund work together.

## Support for philanthropic regranting

Grassroots initiatives use the platform, and foundations and funders can use it too. Through Open Collective, OSE can set up dedicated online funds to:

* Receive donations or grants earmarked for specific causes or regions
* Disburse grants to multiple projects (including informal or unincorporated groups) in a simple, transparent way
* Let funders and the public track how resources are used

Each fund has its own profile page, budget, and update feed, like a Collective. Regranting partners can then easily share their goals, track disbursements, and meet reporting obligations with little extra work.

## Why transparency matters

Transparency is central to the Open Collective platform. When financial information is public, initiatives and funders can:

* Show responsible fund management to donors and stakeholders
* Simplify reporting, because funders can directly monitor how their resources are allocated
* Encourage trust and coordination between grantees and grantmakers

Financial transactions are public, but personal details such as names and email addresses are visible only to authorized admins.

## Key features

The Open Collective platform includes:

* Real-time budget tracking
* Integrated expense and payout tools
* Custom donation tiers and fundraising campaigns
* Event management tools
* Automated monthly financial summaries
* Public updates and communication channels


<!-- opencrane:page -->

# Umbrella organization

Open Source Europe (OSE) provides a shared legal and financial framework for open source projects, developer networks, and software communities.

## Collective infrastructure

OSE is an umbrella organization and the fiscal host for open source initiatives. Each project runs independently on the Open Collective platform, with its own public page and transparent budget. Each project also benefits from the legal standing of a professional Belgian nonprofit (ASBL/vzw).

With this structure, communities can manage funds, pay service providers on compliant invoices, and receive grants. They do not need to run their own legal entity.

***

## Key benefits

Hosting with OSE gives your project the following benefits.

* Your project skips the complexity of nonprofit incorporation, bank account openings, and statutory bookkeeping.
* Foundations, corporations, and public authorities that require a registered nonprofit intermediary can fund your project.
* OSE handles the administrative work, including expense processing, bookkeeping, and annual financial reporting.
* Every transaction is logged in real time, which builds trust with your backers and contributors.
* Your project joins a network of like-minded maintainers and projects in the European open source community.

***

> **Caution:** ## Responsibilities and alignment
>
> To keep the umbrella organization sound, hosted projects must follow three core principles:
>
> * Mission alignment: Projects must actively support the development or sustainability of open source software.
> * Nonprofit compliance: OSE is an ASBL/vzw, so projects must operate within the limits of Belgian law. They must focus on community benefit rather than purely commercial for-profit activities.
> * Operational transparency: Projects must conduct all financial activities through the Open Collective platform to ensure public accountability.

***

## Use cases OSE supports

OSE supports the following use cases:

* Open source libraries: A legal home for critical libraries to receive corporate and individual donations.
* Project ecosystems: One structure for a set of related tools that a distributed community manages.
* Tech communities: Regional developer groups or meetups that manage funds for events, travel stipends, and venues.

***

[Apply to join the umbrella](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply)
